output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true

params:

The flaviLib counterpart of `stall_distributions_v4_20261115.Rmd`. Every subtitle names the file and column
its values came from.

**This is not the viromelib notebook with new paths.** Four structural differences in the data force
different figures, and they are the reason this is a separate file:

| | viromelib (v4) | flaviLib | consequence here |
|---|---|---|---|
| conditions | one | **10 mM and 1 mM, called separately** | every panel carries a `condition` axis; the two are never pooled |
| replicates | 3, gate >= 2 of 3 | 4, gate >= 2 of 4 (`_rep1..rep4`) | replicate columns are detected, not hard-coded |
| regions | 3UTR / inferred_3UTR / intergenic / genome | **only 3UTR and inferred_3UTR** | `region_group` would collapse to one level, so panels split on `region` instead (section 1) |
| families | many | **Flaviviridae / Hepaciviridae / Pestiviridae + a no-family group** | family is a 4-level axis; genus carries the resolution (section 4) |
| tiles | 196 nt, 80 nt step | 196 nt, **20 nt step** | 450 of 699 sites are called in 2+ tiles, against 55 of 391 in viromelib. The confound check (section 9) is a headline caveat, not a footnote |
| accession : virus | 1.16 | **1.61** (439 accessions = 273 TaxIDs) | every count table reports sites, accessions **and** viruses (section 7) |

Figures:

| # | figure | what it shows |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `stop_by_region` | distance from the stop codon, annotated 3'UTR vs inferred 3'UTR, per condition |
| 2 | `stop_by_family` | distance from the stop codon, the three families, per condition |
| 3 | `sf_by_condition` | stall fraction, 10 mM vs 1 mM, over all sites (composition effect — read section 8 first) |
| 4 | `sf_by_family`, `sf_by_genus` | stall fraction by family and by genus |
| 5 | `sf_by_cm_class` | stall fraction by CM class (seven models) |
| 6 | `sf_by_host` | stall fraction by host group — **skipped unless the host table exists** |
| 7 | `counts_by_family` | sites / accessions / viruses per family and genus |
| 8 | `condition_overlap` | sites called in one condition only (the step 13b result) |
| 9 | — | confound check: stall fraction against position in tile |
| 10 | — | sensitivity: adjacent sites at merge distance 0 (the open decision) |

**What the notebook does not do:** it applies no gate of its own. Every row of `.sites.csv` already passed
all v7.3 gates in >= 2 of 4 replicates (`min_reps_passing 2`, `min_median_sf 0.3`, `max_meta_qvalue 0.01`,
`merge_distance 0`), and one row is one site, not one tile.

**Inputs**, all in `params$input_dir`. Required:

| file | gives |
|---|---|
| `261021_flaviLib_150x150_10mM.sites.csv` | 699 sites |
| `261021_flaviLib_150x150_01mM.sites.csv` | 459 sites |
| `261021_flaviLib_150x150_<COND>.tile_rows.csv` | sections 9 and 11 |

Optional; the section that needs each one is skipped, with a printed note, if it is absent:

| file | gives | produced by |
|---|---|---|
| `MANIFEST.tsv` | `taxid` -> the virus (TaxID) counts | `fetch_genbank_snapshot.py`, flaviLib step 11g |
| `virus_taxonomy_flaviLib_261021.csv` | `lowest_group`, for the 145 accessions with no genus | step 11h |
| `*_<COND>.sites_stopdist.csv` | `distance_from_stop` (sections 1 and 2) | `stall_distance_to_stop.py` — **not yet run for flaviLib** |
| `host_by_accession_<date>.tsv` | host group (section 6) | `host_from_records.py` — **not yet run for flaviLib** |
| `pair_conditions_sf_261021.tsv` | the point-to-point Mg2+ pairing (section 8) | `pair_conditions_sf.py`, step 13b |
| `band_counts_flaviLib.csv` | detectability bands (section 7) | `detectability_floor.py`, step 13c |

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)
library(svglite)
# error = TRUE: a chunk that fails prints its error into the HTML and the knit CONTINUES, so one run
# names every problem instead of stopping at the first. Set back to FALSE once the notebook is known
# good, so that a real failure is not quietly tolerated.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, error = TRUE)
```

## 1. Config

```{r config}
INPUT_DIR <- path.expand(params$input_dir)
OUTDIR    <- path.expand(params$outdir)
dir.create(OUTDIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

PREFIX <- "261021_flaviLib_150x150"
# Order matters: it sets the factor level order, so 10 mM is the reference everywhere.
CONDITIONS  <- c("10mM", "01mM")
COND_LABELS <- c("10mM" = "10 mM Mg2+", "01mM" = "1 mM Mg2+")
cond_colors <- c("10 mM Mg2+" = "#B2182B", "1 mM Mg2+" = "#2166AC")

sites_path <- function(cond) file.path(INPUT_DIR, glue("{PREFIX}_{cond}.sites.csv"))
tiles_path <- function(cond) file.path(INPUT_DIR, glue("{PREFIX}_{cond}.tile_rows.csv"))
stop_path  <- function(cond) file.path(INPUT_DIR, glue("{PREFIX}_{cond}.sites_stopdist.csv"))

MANIFEST_TSV <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "MANIFEST.tsv")
TAX_CSV      <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "virus_taxonomy_flaviLib_261021.csv")
HOST_MAP_TSV <- Sys.glob(file.path(INPUT_DIR, "host_by_accession_*.tsv"))[1]
PAIRING_TSV  <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "pair_conditions_sf_261021.tsv")
BANDS_CSV    <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "band_counts_flaviLib.csv")

FIG_W <- 9; FIG_H <- 6
MIN_GROUP_N <- 5        # family / genus groups smaller than this are pooled
HOST_MIN_N  <- 3        # host groups smaller than this are pooled
HOST_LEVEL  <- "fine"   # "fine" or "broad"
MERGE_NT    <- 1        # section 10 sensitivity. 1 nt, not viromelib's 3: at a 20 nt tile step the
                        # question raised by the flaviLib log is specifically the 66 pairs within 1 nt
SUBSET_FAMILIES   <- c("Flaviviridae")
SUBSET_HOST_MIN_N <- 2

# The no-family group is 21 of 699 sites at 10 mM (jingmenviruses, the Shi-et-al. invertebrate viromes,
# Fluviflavili virus, Gentian Kobu-sho-associated virus). The flaviLib log is explicit that a family-level
# panel must either show them as a labelled group or state that it drops them -- they must not vanish
# silently. So this label is assigned explicitly and PROTECTED from small-group pooling below.
FAMILY_NA_LABEL <- "no family assigned"
GENUS_NA_LABEL  <- "no genus assigned"
# Step 20e measured 32 of 319 site accessions with no host from either source (10 %), against 0 of 286 in
# viromelib, because Virus-Host DB is keyed on RefSeq and 184 of flaviLib's 439 accessions are not NC_
# records. So unlike viromelib this notebook MUST show a no-host group rather than quietly coalescing it
# to "Unknown" and letting pool_small fold it away. Labelled, protected from pooling, and counted.
HOST_NA_LABEL <- "no host assigned"
family_colors <- c("Flaviviridae" = "#B2182B", "Hepaciviridae" = "#2166AC",
                   "Pestiviridae" = "#1B7837", "no family assigned" = "#8C8C8C")

# Seven CMs (decision 3). class1c sits next to 1a/1b deliberately: it is a SUBCLASS of class 1, not a
# seventh tier (decision 18), and decision 28 -- which CM columns a figure displays -- is still open.
# Set CM_GROUP_CLASS1 to TRUE to collapse 1a/1b/1c into one "Class 1" level and see the other reading.
CM_GROUP_CLASS1 <- FALSE
CM_COLS <- c(class1a  = "CL_Class_1a_xrRNA_final.cm_hit",
             class1b  = "CL_Class_1b_xrRNA_final.cm_hit",
             class1c  = "class1c.cm_hit",
             class2   = "CL_Class_2_xrRNA_final.cm_hit",
             class3   = "cl3_NAR_2025.align.mpkadded.edited.confident.dedup.IDcurated.SS_cons.cm_hit",
             class4   = "class4_cl4_v9_20260824.cm_hit",
             dumbbell = "dumbbell_RF00525.cm_hit")
cm_labels <- c(class1a = "Class 1a", class1b = "Class 1b", class1c = "Class 1c",
               class2 = "Class 2", class3 = "Class 3", class4 = "Class 4",
               dumbbell = "Dumbbell", no_hit = "No hit")
cm_colors <- c("Class 1a" = "#7D80DA", "Class 1b" = "#150578", "Class 1c" = "#3F48CC",
               "Class 2" = "#7FDEFF", "Class 3" = "#9CBFA7", "Class 4" = "#EA9010",
               "Dumbbell" = "#8C564B", "Class 1" = "#150578", "No hit" = "#8C8C8C")

# flaviLib has no intergenic and no whole-genome features, so a stall's distance from the stop codon is
# comparable across the library EXCEPT for one construction difference: parse.py pads an inferred 3'UTR
# with 50 nt of upstream CDS, so its offset 0 lies inside the CDS, while an annotated 3UTR feature starts
# at the GenBank 3'UTR boundary with no buffer. Distance-from-stop panels therefore split on this.
region_colors <- c("3UTR" = "#1B7837", "inferred_3UTR" = "#7FBF7B")
REGION_LABELS <- c("3UTR" = "annotated 3'UTR", "inferred_3UTR" = "inferred 3'UTR (50 nt CDS buffer)")
STOP_XLIM <- c(-100, 900)
```

## 2. Load both conditions

```{r preflight}
# Every path this notebook can use, and whether it is there. Only the two sites tables are required; an
# absent optional file disables its own section and nothing else. Checked before any reading, so a
# mistyped or renamed download is named here rather than surfacing as an obscure error 200 lines later.
pf <- tibble(
  file = c(map_chr(CONDITIONS, sites_path), map_chr(CONDITIONS, tiles_path),
           MANIFEST_TSV, TAX_CSV, map_chr(CONDITIONS, stop_path),
           if (is.na(HOST_MAP_TSV)) NA_character_ else HOST_MAP_TSV, PAIRING_TSV, BANDS_CSV),
  required = c(rep(TRUE, length(CONDITIONS)), rep(FALSE, length(CONDITIONS)),
               FALSE, FALSE, rep(FALSE, length(CONDITIONS)), FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),
  enables = c(rep("everything", length(CONDITIONS)), rep("sections 9 and 11", length(CONDITIONS)),
              "virus (TaxID) counts", "genus fallback (lowest_group)",
              rep("sections 1, 2 and the no-hit window", length(CONDITIONS)),
              "sections 6 and 7 (host)", "section 8 paired panels", "detectability bands")) %>%
  mutate(present = !is.na(file) & file.exists(file),
         name = if_else(is.na(file), "(no host_by_accession_*.tsv found)", basename(file)))
cat("input directory:", INPUT_DIR, "\n\n")
print(pf %>% select(name, required, present, enables) %>% as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)

miss <- pf %>% filter(required, !present)
if (nrow(miss)) {
  stop("missing required input", if (nrow(miss) > 1) "s" else "", ":\n  ",
       paste(basename(miss$file), collapse = "\n  "),
       "\n\nfiles actually present in ", INPUT_DIR, ":\n  ",
       paste(list.files(INPUT_DIR), collapse = "\n  "),
       "\n\nnames are built from PREFIX in the config chunk, so a renamed download ",
       "(e.g. a ' (1)' suffix) will not be found.")
}
if (any(!pf$present)) {
  cat("\nskipping, because the file above is absent:\n  ",
      paste(pf$enables[!pf$present], collapse = "\n   "), "\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r load}
# The sites table carries `organism` TWICE (columns 7 and 17): apply_publication_cutoffs.py writes it from
# the snapshot manifest and it is also passed through from the annotation. Checked on the 261021 tables:
# the two copies are byte-identical in all 699 + 459 rows. Kept as an assertion rather than an assumption.
read_sites_one <- function(cond) {
  p <- sites_path(cond)
  stopifnot("sites file not found" = file.exists(p))
  s <- suppressWarnings(read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal"))
  for (nm in unique(names(s)[duplicated(names(s))])) {
    cp <- s[, names(s) == nm, drop = FALSE]
    stopifnot("duplicated columns differ in content" =
                all(map_lgl(cp[-1], ~ identical(as.character(.x), as.character(cp[[1]])))))
    cat(glue("{cond}: duplicated column '{nm}', {ncol(cp)} identical copies, one kept"), "\n")
  }
  s <- s[, !duplicated(names(s))]
  s$condition <- cond
  s
}
sites_raw <- map(set_names(CONDITIONS), read_sites_one)
walk2(names(sites_raw), sites_raw, ~ cat(.x, ":", nrow(.y), "sites,", ncol(.y), "columns\n"))

# bind_rows tolerates a column present in one condition and not the other; warn rather than silently fill.
only_in <- map(sites_raw, names)
if (length(setdiff(union(only_in[[1]], only_in[[2]]), intersect(only_in[[1]], only_in[[2]]))))
  cat("NOTE columns not shared by both conditions:",
      paste(setdiff(union(only_in[[1]], only_in[[2]]), intersect(only_in[[1]], only_in[[2]])),
            collapse = ", "), "\n")
sites <- bind_rows(sites_raw)

SF_COL   <- c("median_treated_sf", "median_sf", "treated_sf", "sf")[
             c("median_treated_sf", "median_sf", "treated_sf", "sf") %in% names(sites)][1]
REPS_COL <- c("max_n_reps_passing", "n_reps_passing", "n_reps")[
             c("max_n_reps_passing", "n_reps_passing", "n_reps") %in% names(sites)][1]
N_REPS   <- length(grep("^treated_sf_rep[0-9]+$", names(sites)))
cat("stall fraction column:", SF_COL, "| replicate column:", REPS_COL,
    "| replicates detected:", N_REPS, "\n")
stopifnot("expected 4 replicates for flaviLib" = N_REPS == 4)
stopifnot("positional columns are required" =
  all(c("stall_site_genomic_position", "genome_length", "feature_genomic_start", "feature_genomic_end",
        "feature_length", "stall_offset_in_feature", "region", "site_id", "plain_accession",
        "tile_start", "tile_end", "stall_position") %in% names(sites)))
# viromelib dropped whole-genome features at load. flaviLib has none; assert rather than carry the code.
stopifnot("unexpected whole-genome feature in flaviLib" = !any(sites$region == "genome"))
```

```{r derive}
NO_HIT <- c("", "nan", "na", "none", "false", "0", "no", "null")
is_hit <- function(x) { v <- str_trim(str_to_lower(as.character(x))); !is.na(v) & !(v %in% NO_HIT) }
for (k in names(CM_COLS)) sites[[paste0("hit_", k)]] <-
  if (CM_COLS[[k]] %in% names(sites)) is_hit(sites[[CM_COLS[[k]]]]) else FALSE
missing_cm <- names(CM_COLS)[!CM_COLS %in% names(sites)]
if (length(missing_cm)) cat("CM columns absent from the table:", paste(missing_cm, collapse = ", "), "\n")

d <- sites %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(unname(COND_LABELS[condition]), levels = unname(COND_LABELS[CONDITIONS])),
    region    = factor(region, levels = names(region_colors)),
    region_lab = factor(unname(REGION_LABELS[as.character(region)]), levels = unname(REGION_LABELS)),
    family = coalesce(na_if(na_if(as.character(family), "nan"), ""), FAMILY_NA_LABEL),
    genus  = coalesce(na_if(na_if(as.character(genus), "nan"), ""), GENUS_NA_LABEL),
    organism = coalesce(na_if(as.character(organism), ""), plain_accession),
    sf = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[SF_COL]])),
    reps_passing = suppressWarnings(as.integer(.data[[REPS_COL]])),
    # positional axes
    rel_genome         = stall_site_genomic_position / genome_length,
    nt_from_genome_end = genome_length - stall_site_genomic_position,
    offset_in_feature  = stall_offset_in_feature,          # NOT the distance from the stop codon
    nt_from_feature_end = feature_genomic_end - stall_site_genomic_position,
    rel_feature        = stall_offset_in_feature / feature_length,
    # tile geometry, for section 9. treated_sf = stall reads / reads assigned to the tile, so the
    # denominator shrinks as the stall approaches the tile 3' end.
    nt_after_stall     = tile_end - stall_position,
    # one CM class per site, priority 1a > 1b > 1c > 2 > 3 > 4 > dumbbell
    cm_key = case_when(hit_class1a ~ "class1a", hit_class1b ~ "class1b", hit_class1c ~ "class1c",
                       hit_class2 ~ "class2", hit_class3 ~ "class3", hit_class4 ~ "class4",
                       hit_dumbbell ~ "dumbbell", TRUE ~ "no_hit"),
    cm_key = if (CM_GROUP_CLASS1) str_replace(cm_key, "^class1[abc]$", "class1") else cm_key)
cm_lab_used <- if (CM_GROUP_CLASS1)
  c(class1 = "Class 1", cm_labels[!names(cm_labels) %in% c("class1a","class1b","class1c")]) else cm_labels
d <- d %>% mutate(cm_class = factor(unname(cm_lab_used[cm_key]), levels = unname(cm_lab_used)))

cat("\nsites per condition:\n"); print(d %>% count(condition, name = "n_sites"))
cat("\nby region:\n"); print(d %>% count(condition, region, name = "n_sites"))
cat("\nby CM class:\n"); print(d %>% count(condition, cm_class, name = "n_sites") %>%
                               pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n_sites, values_fill = 0))
cat("\nby replicates passing (of", N_REPS, "):\n")
print(d %>% count(condition, reps_passing) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n, values_fill = 0))
```

```{r taxid}
# accession : virus is 1.61 here (439 accessions, 273 TaxIDs) because segmented jingmenviruses contribute
# one accession per segment. Every count in this notebook therefore has to say which unit it uses, and
# "viruses" needs the TaxID, which the sites table does not carry. MANIFEST.tsv does.
HAS_TAXID <- file.exists(MANIFEST_TSV)
if (HAS_TAXID) {
  mani <- read_tsv(MANIFEST_TSV, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
    transmute(acc_nover = str_remove(accession, "\\..*$"), taxid,
              organism_manifest = organism) %>% distinct(acc_nover, .keep_all = TRUE)
  d <- d %>% mutate(acc_nover = str_remove(plain_accession, "\\..*$")) %>%
    left_join(mani, by = "acc_nover")
  cat("MANIFEST.tsv:", nrow(mani), "accessions |",
      sum(is.na(d$taxid)), "site rows with no TaxID\n")
  cat("site accessions:", n_distinct(d$plain_accession),
      "| site viruses (TaxID):", n_distinct(d$taxid), "\n")
} else {
  d$taxid <- NA_character_
  cat("NOT FOUND:", MANIFEST_TSV,
      "\n  virus (TaxID) counts are reported as NA. Copy MANIFEST.tsv from",
      "data/genbank_snapshot_flaviLib_261021/.\n")
}

HAS_TAX <- file.exists(TAX_CSV)
if (HAS_TAX) {
  tax <- read_csv(TAX_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    select(acc_nover = accession, lowest_group = any_of("lowest_group")) %>%
    mutate(acc_nover = str_remove(acc_nover, "\\..*$")) %>% distinct(acc_nover, .keep_all = TRUE)
  d <- d %>% left_join(tax, by = "acc_nover")
  # Panel D of the flaviLib log is by genus with lowest_group where no genus is assigned (the
  # Jingmenvirus group is unranked, so it has no genus node to fall back on).
  d <- d %>% mutate(genus_group = if_else(genus == GENUS_NA_LABEL,
                                          coalesce(lowest_group, GENUS_NA_LABEL), genus))
  cat("taxonomy:", basename(TAX_CSV), "| genus filled from lowest_group for",
      sum(d$genus == GENUS_NA_LABEL & d$genus_group != GENUS_NA_LABEL), "site rows\n")
} else {
  d$genus_group <- d$genus
  cat("NOT FOUND:", TAX_CSV, "\n  genus panel uses `genus` only;",
      sum(d$genus == GENUS_NA_LABEL), "site rows stay '", GENUS_NA_LABEL, "'.\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r host}
HAS_HOST <- !is.na(HOST_MAP_TSV) && file.exists(HOST_MAP_TSV)
if (HAS_HOST) {
  hm <- read_tsv(HOST_MAP_TSV, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
    transmute(acc_nover = str_remove(plain_accession, "\\..*$"),
              host_broad = na_if(host_broad, ""), host_fine = na_if(host_fine, ""),
              host_fine_all = if ("host_fine_all" %in% names(.)) na_if(host_fine_all, "") else NA_character_,
              host_confidence, sample_host_flag)
  d <- d %>% left_join(hm, by = "acc_nover")
  cat("host table:", basename(HOST_MAP_TSV), "\n"); print(table(d$host_confidence, useNA = "ifany"))
  d <- d %>% mutate(
    host_fine_all = coalesce(host_fine_all, host_fine),
    host_group = if (HOST_LEVEL == "fine") coalesce(host_fine, host_broad, HOST_NA_LABEL)
                 else coalesce(host_broad, HOST_NA_LABEL),
    host_split = if (HOST_LEVEL == "fine") coalesce(host_fine_all, host_broad, HOST_NA_LABEL)
                 else coalesce(host_broad, HOST_NA_LABEL),
    multi_host = str_detect(host_split, fixed(" + ")))
  cat("\nhost level:", HOST_LEVEL, "| site rows with more than one host group:", sum(d$multi_host), "\n")
  print(sort(table(d$host_group), decreasing = TRUE))
  # Coverage, per condition and in accessions, because a 10 % hostless rate is a caveat on every host
  # panel and the figure legend has to carry it.
  cov <- d %>% group_by(condition) %>%
    summarise(sites = n(), sites_no_host = sum(host_group == HOST_NA_LABEL),
              accessions = n_distinct(plain_accession),
              accessions_no_host = n_distinct(plain_accession[host_group == HOST_NA_LABEL]),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pct_sites_no_host = round(100 * sites_no_host / sites, 1))
  cat("\nhost coverage (step 20e v1 measured 32 of 319 site accessions with no host):\n")
  print(cov)
  write_csv(cov, file.path(OUTDIR, "host_coverage.csv"))
} else {
  d <- d %>% mutate(host_group = HOST_NA_LABEL, host_split = HOST_NA_LABEL,
                    host_fine_all = NA_character_, multi_host = FALSE)
  cat("NO HOST TABLE in", INPUT_DIR, "\n  Section 6 is skipped and host does not appear in section 7.\n",
      "  flaviLib has no step 20 yet. See the commands at the end of this notebook:",
      "host_from_records.py\n  reads data/genbank_snapshot_flaviLib_261021/ directly, and 362 of the 439",
      "records carry a\n  /host qualifier, so the axis is worth producing.\n")
}
# one row per site per host group, for every host-split plot
expand_hosts <- function(df) {
  if (!HAS_HOST) return(df %>% mutate(host_one = NA_character_))
  df %>% separate_rows(host_split, sep = " \\+ ") %>% rename(host_one = host_split)
}
```

```{r stopdist}
# stall_distance_to_stop.py has not been run for flaviLib. When it is, drop the two CSVs in and
# sections 1 and 2 appear with no other change.
stop_files <- map_chr(CONDITIONS, stop_path)
HAS_STOP <- all(file.exists(stop_files))
if (HAS_STOP) {
  sd <- map2_dfr(CONDITIONS, stop_files, function(cond, p) {
    x <- suppressWarnings(read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal"))
    x <- x[, !duplicated(names(x))]
    stopifnot("stopdist file has no distance_from_stop column" = "distance_from_stop" %in% names(x))
    x %>% select(site_id, distance_from_stop,
                 any_of(c("cds_id", "cds_product", "stop_codon", "flags"))) %>%
      mutate(condition = factor(unname(COND_LABELS[cond]),
                                levels = unname(COND_LABELS[CONDITIONS])))
  })
  # site_id repeats across conditions, so the join key must include condition.
  d <- d %>% left_join(sd, by = c("site_id", "condition"))
  n_stop <- sum(!is.na(d$distance_from_stop))
  cat("stopdist joined:", n_stop, "of", nrow(d), "site rows\n")
  print(summary(d$distance_from_stop))
  # The file existing is not the same as the join matching. The key is site_id + condition, and a
  # stopdist table written for one condition, or with site_ids from a different gating run, joins to
  # nothing and leaves every distance NA -- which then empties the facets rather than failing cleanly.
  if (n_stop == 0) {
    cat("\nWARNING the stopdist files exist but NOTHING joined, so sections 1, 2 and the no-hit window\n",
        "  table are skipped. The join key is site_id + condition. Compare the two sides:\n", sep = "")
    cat("  sites   site_id examples:", paste(head(unique(d$site_id), 3), collapse = " | "), "\n")
    cat("  stopdist site_id examples:", paste(head(unique(sd$site_id), 3), collapse = " | "), "\n")
    cat("  sites   conditions:", paste(levels(droplevels(d$condition)), collapse = " | "), "\n")
    cat("  stopdist conditions:", paste(sort(unique(as.character(sd$condition))), collapse = " | "), "\n")
    cat("  overlap on site_id alone:", length(intersect(d$site_id, sd$site_id)), "of",
        n_distinct(d$site_id), "\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("NOT FOUND:", paste(basename(stop_files[!file.exists(stop_files)]), collapse = ", "),
      "\n  Sections 1 and 2 are skipped. Produce them with stall_distance_to_stop.py",
      "(see the commands at the end).\n")
  d$distance_from_stop <- NA_real_
  n_stop <- 0L
}
# What the stop-distance sections are gated on: data, not a file. A facet on an empty frame throws
# "Faceting variables must have at least one value" rather than skipping.
HAS_STOP_DATA <- n_stop > 0
cat("stop-distance sections", if (HAS_STOP_DATA) "WILL" else "will NOT", "be drawn\n")
```

```{r helpers}
OTHER <- "Other (small groups)"
# `protect` is the difference from the viromelib version: FAMILY_NA_LABEL must survive pooling even at
# n = 4 (1 mM), because "21 sites with no family" is a stated finding, not a rounding error.
pool_small <- function(x, n_min = MIN_GROUP_N, protect = character()) {
  keep <- union(names(which(table(x) >= n_min)), protect)
  f <- factor(ifelse(x %in% keep, as.character(x), OTHER))
  if (OTHER %in% levels(f)) fct_relevel(f, OTHER, after = Inf) else f
}
# lab_n appends "(n=...)" to a factor level. Use it ONLY on an unfaceted axis: inside a condition facet it
# would count over both conditions and so label each panel with the pooled n. Faceted panels therefore
# carry plain levels and the per-condition n goes to the CSV written beside each figure.
lab_n <- function(x) { x <- droplevels(as.factor(x)); tb <- table(x)
  factor(paste0(levels(x), " (n=", as.integer(tb[levels(x)]), ")")[as.integer(x)],
         levels = paste0(levels(x), " (n=", as.integer(tb[levels(x)]), ")")) }
# Builds the plot before writing it, so a figure whose data is empty -- the usual cause being a facet
# variable with no values -- is reported BY NAME and skipped instead of aborting the knit inside ggsave().
save_fig <- function(p, name, w = FIG_W, h = FIG_H) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ ggplot2::ggplot_build(p); TRUE },
                 error = function(e) {
                   cat("FIGURE NOT DRAWN:", name, "::", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); FALSE })
  if (!ok) return(invisible(NULL))
  ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(name, ".pdf")), p, width = w, height = h, device = cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(name, ".svg")), p, width = w, height = h); invisible(p) }
theme_fl <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40"),
        strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#F0F0F0", linewidth = 0.3))

SRC_SITES <- glue("{PREFIX}_<COND>.sites.csv")
SRC_HOST  <- if (HAS_HOST) basename(HOST_MAP_TSV) else "(no host table)"
SRC_STOP  <- glue("{PREFIX}_<COND>.sites_stopdist.csv")
src_line  <- function(...) paste0("source: ", paste0(..., collapse = ""))

dd  <- d %>% filter(!is.na(sf))                                  # one row per site
dh  <- expand_hosts(d)  %>% mutate(host_one = if (HAS_HOST) pool_small(host_one, HOST_MIN_N, protect = HOST_NA_LABEL) else host_one)
ddh <- expand_hosts(dd) %>% mutate(host_one = if (HAS_HOST) pool_small(host_one, HOST_MIN_N, protect = HOST_NA_LABEL) else host_one)
cat(nrow(d), "site rows |", nrow(dd), "with a stall fraction |", nrow(dh), "site-by-host rows\n")
# What each figure draws from, and which sections are on. A zero row count here is the cause of
# "Faceting variables must have at least one value", and this names the frame before any figure runs.
cat("\nframes the figures use:\n")
print(data.frame(frame = c("d (all sites)", "dd (with a stall fraction)", "dh (site x host)",
                           "ddh (site x host, with SF)"),
                 rows = c(nrow(d), nrow(dd), nrow(dh), nrow(ddh))), row.names = FALSE)
cat("condition levels with data:", paste(levels(droplevels(d$condition)), collapse = " | "), "\n")
cat("gates: HAS_STOP", HAS_STOP, "| HAS_STOP_DATA", HAS_STOP_DATA, "| HAS_HOST", HAS_HOST,
    "| HAS_TAXID", HAS_TAXID, "| HAS_TAX", HAS_TAX, "\n")
cat("distance_from_stop non-missing:", sum(!is.na(d$distance_from_stop)), "of", nrow(d), "\n")
cat("THIS NOTEBOOK IS", basename(knitr::current_input()), "\n")
```

## 3. Figures

### 1. Distance from the stop codon — annotated vs inferred 3'UTR

Split on `region` rather than on viromelib's `region_group`: flaviLib has no intergenic and no whole-genome
features, so `region_group` has a single level and the viromelib facet would be an empty distinction. The
split that *does* matter here is how the zero point was obtained. An annotated `3UTR` feature begins at the
GenBank 3'UTR boundary, which assumes the UTR starts immediately after the stop codon; an `inferred_3UTR`
begins 50 nt inside the CDS, so its offsets 0–49 are CDS and a stall there is reported at a negative
distance by construction.

```{r fig1-stop-region, eval=HAS_STOP_DATA, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
ds <- d %>% filter(!is.na(distance_from_stop))
f1 <- ds %>% filter(between(distance_from_stop, STOP_XLIM[1], STOP_XLIM[2])) %>%
  ggplot(aes(distance_from_stop, colour = condition, fill = condition)) +
  geom_density(adjust = 0.6, linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.5, length = unit(0.03, "npc")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cond_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cond_colors, name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ lab_n(region_lab), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Distance from the stop codon, by feature type and Mg2+ condition",
       subtitle = str_wrap(glue(
         "density, area = 1 per curve. 0 = first base after the stop codon; negative = inside the CDS. ",
         "An inferred 3'UTR carries a 50 nt CDS buffer (parse.py), so negative values there are expected; ",
         "an annotated 3UTR has no buffer. Rug marks individual sites. ",
         "{src_line('distance_from_stop from ', SRC_STOP, ', region from ', SRC_SITES)}"), 115),
       x = "distance from stop codon (nt)", y = "density") +
  theme_fl
save_fig(f1, "stop_by_region", w = 9, h = 6); f1

stop_tab <- ds %>% group_by(condition, region) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median = median(distance_from_stop), q25 = quantile(distance_from_stop, .25),
            q75 = quantile(distance_from_stop, .75), min = min(distance_from_stop),
            n_negative = sum(distance_from_stop < 0),
            median_feature_length = median(feature_length), .groups = "drop")
write_csv(stop_tab, file.path(OUTDIR, "stop_by_region.csv")); knitr::kable(stop_tab)
for (rg in levels(droplevels(ds$region))) {
  x <- ds %>% filter(region == rg) %>% mutate(g = droplevels(condition))
  if (nlevels(x$g) == 2 && min(table(x$g)) >= 3)
    cat(rg, ": Mann-Whitney across conditions p =",
        signif(wilcox.test(distance_from_stop ~ g, data = x)$p.value, 3), "\n")
}
```

### 2. Distance from the stop codon — by family

viromelib's equivalent panel contrasted the flaviviruses with two plant families. flaviLib has no plant
families, so the comparison that exists here is between its three: *Flaviviridae*, *Hepaciviridae*,
*Pestiviridae*. The no-family group is kept and labelled.

```{r fig2-stop-family, eval=HAS_STOP_DATA, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
f2 <- ds %>% filter(between(distance_from_stop, STOP_XLIM[1], STOP_XLIM[2])) %>%
  mutate(fam = factor(family, levels = names(family_colors))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(distance_from_stop, colour = fam, fill = fam)) +
  geom_density(adjust = 0.6, linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.4, length = unit(0.03, "npc")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = family_colors, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = family_colors, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ lab_n(condition), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Distance from the stop codon, by family",
       subtitle = str_wrap(glue(
         "density, area = 1 per curve. The 'no family assigned' group is 21 of 699 sites at 10 mM ",
         "(jingmenviruses, unplaced invertebrate viromes) and is shown rather than dropped. ",
         "{src_line('distance_from_stop from ', SRC_STOP, ', family from ', SRC_SITES)}"), 115),
       x = "distance from stop codon (nt)", y = "density") +
  theme_fl
save_fig(f2, "stop_by_family", w = 9, h = 6); f2
write_csv(ds %>% group_by(condition, family) %>%
            summarise(n = n(), median = median(distance_from_stop),
                      q25 = quantile(distance_from_stop, .25),
                      q75 = quantile(distance_from_stop, .75), .groups = "drop"),
          file.path(OUTDIR, "stop_by_family.csv"))
```

### 3. Stall fraction, 10 mM vs 1 mM

**Read section 8 before reading this panel.** These are two different site sets — 699 and 459 sites, with
only part of each shared — so the difference between the two boxes mixes the Mg2+ effect with which sites
passed. The flaviLib log measured that directly: unpaired medians 0.588 and 0.404, but a median *paired*
delta of only −0.029. The panel is drawn because it is the comparison a reader expects to see, and
annotated with the paired figure so it cannot be read as a per-site effect.

```{r fig3-sf-condition, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
paired_note <- if (file.exists(PAIRING_TSV)) "see section 8 for the paired comparison" else
  "paired comparison not available: pair_conditions_sf.py output is absent (see section 8)"
f3 <- dd %>% ggplot(aes(condition, sf, fill = condition)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0, width = 0.12, size = 1.1, alpha = 0.35, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cond_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
  labs(title = "Stall fraction by Mg2+ condition — UNPAIRED, two different site sets",
       subtitle = str_wrap(glue(
         "one row per site; {nrow(filter(dd, condition == levels(dd$condition)[1]))} vs ",
         "{nrow(filter(dd, condition == levels(dd$condition)[2]))} sites, overlapping only in part, so ",
         "this contrast is partly composition and not a per-site change. {paired_note}. ",
         "{src_line(SF_COL, ' from ', SRC_SITES)}"), 110),
       x = NULL, y = "stall fraction") +
  theme_fl
save_fig(f3, "sf_by_condition", w = 7, h = 5); f3
knitr::kable(dd %>% group_by(condition) %>%
               summarise(n = n(), median = round(median(sf), 4), q25 = round(quantile(sf, .25), 4),
                         q75 = round(quantile(sf, .75), 4), .groups = "drop"))
```

```{r bands, eval=file.exists(BANDS_CSV)}
# Detectability floor (step 13c): 9 of 439 accessions cannot support a "not detected" claim and 28 more
# are uninformative. Passing sites are all above the floor by construction, so this changes confidence in
# ABSENCES, not in these detections -- but a figure whose denominator is "all 439" needs the bands.
bands <- read_csv(BANDS_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(bands)
cat("The floor affects absences, not the sites plotted above: every passing site sits above it by\n",
    "construction, since the floor is the minimum over passing sites.\n")
```

## 4. Section 8 — Mg2+ dependence: loss of sites, not graded weakening

The flaviLib log's step 13b result: per-site stall fraction barely moves (median paired delta −0.029) while
**337 sites are lost at 1 mM against 111 gained**. So the effect is whether a site is called at all, and
section 3's boxes are the wrong way to show it.

The pairing itself is `pair_conditions_sf.py`'s job and is not reimplemented here, because its matching rule
is not reproducible from the sites tables alone: it reads the stall fraction of the failing side from
`peaks_annotated.csv` (where candidate rows survive for sites that failed the gates), and it requires
`stall_reads >= 10` on both ends. A naive overlap on `(accession, stall_site_genomic_position)` with a 1 nt
tolerance over the two sites tables gives **316 / 78 / 383** (10 mM only / 1 mM only / both), against the
script's **337 / 111 / 336** — the two do not agree, and the script's numbers are the ones to quote. The
block below prints the naive overlap only as a labelled cross-check on which sites are shared.

```{r pairing}
if (file.exists(PAIRING_TSV)) {
  pr <- read_tsv(PAIRING_TSV, show_col_types = FALSE)
  cat("pairing table:", basename(PAIRING_TSV), nrow(pr), "rows\n")
  if ("pair_class" %in% names(pr)) print(pr %>% count(pair_class, name = "n"))
  write_csv(pr, file.path(OUTDIR, "pair_conditions_sf.csv"))
} else {
  cat("NOT FOUND:", PAIRING_TSV,
      "\n  Run pair_conditions_sf.py (step 13b) and drop its output here to get the paired panels.\n\n")
}

# Labelled cross-check, NOT the step 13b numbers.
key <- d %>% transmute(condition, plain_accession,
                       pos = as.integer(round(stall_site_genomic_position)), site_id, sf, cm_class, family)
k1 <- key %>% filter(condition == levels(key$condition)[1])
k2 <- key %>% filter(condition == levels(key$condition)[2])
TOL <- 1
matched_1 <- k1 %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(in_other = any(k2$plain_accession == plain_accession & abs(k2$pos - pos) <= TOL)) %>% ungroup()
matched_2 <- k2 %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(in_other = any(k1$plain_accession == plain_accession & abs(k1$pos - pos) <= TOL)) %>% ungroup()
ov <- tibble(set = c(glue("{levels(key$condition)[1]} only"), glue("{levels(key$condition)[2]} only"),
                     "matched in both (from the 10 mM side)"),
             n = c(sum(!matched_1$in_other), sum(!matched_2$in_other), sum(matched_1$in_other)))
knitr::kable(ov, caption = glue(
  "Naive overlap on (accession, stall_site_genomic_position) at tolerance {TOL} nt. ",
  "NOT the step 13b figures (337 / 111 / 336) -- pair_conditions_sf.py uses a different universe and a ",
  "stall-read requirement. Quote the script, not this table."))
write_csv(bind_rows(matched_1 %>% mutate(side = levels(key$condition)[1]),
                    matched_2 %>% mutate(side = levels(key$condition)[2])),
          file.path(OUTDIR, "condition_overlap_naive.csv"))

f8 <- ov %>% filter(set != "matched in both (from the 10 mM side)") %>%
  ggplot(aes(set, n, fill = set)) + geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(cond_colors), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "Sites called in one condition only",
       subtitle = str_wrap(glue(
         "What moves between conditions is whether a site is called, not its stall fraction. ",
         "These are the naive-overlap counts; pair_conditions_sf.py reports 337 and 111. ",
         "{src_line('both ', SRC_SITES)}"), 110),
       x = NULL, y = "sites") + theme_fl
save_fig(f8, "condition_overlap", w = 7, h = 5); f8
```

## 5. Section 9 — Confound check: stall fraction depends on where the stall sits in its tile

`treated_sf` = stall reads / all reads assigned to the tile, so the denominator shrinks as the stall nears
the tile 3' end. **This matters more in flaviLib than in viromelib**: at a 20 nt tile step, 450 of 699 sites
at 10 mM (and 280 of 459 at 1 mM) are called in two or more tiles, up to nine, against 55 of 391 in
viromelib. Sections 4–6 are all stall fraction, so check this before reading any of them as biology.

```{r confound}
confound_test <- function(df, grp, label, cond) {
  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[grp]]), !is.na(nt_after_stall)) %>%
    mutate(g = droplevels(as.factor(.data[[grp]])))
  if (nlevels(df$g) < 2) return(tibble(condition = cond, grouping = label, n = nrow(df),
                                       n_groups = nlevels(df$g)))
  a <- anova(lm(rank(sf) ~ rank(nt_after_stall), data = df),
             lm(rank(sf) ~ rank(nt_after_stall) + g, data = df))
  tibble(condition = cond, grouping = label, n = nrow(df), n_groups = nlevels(df$g),
         p_sf_differs = kruskal.test(sf ~ g, data = df)$p.value,
         p_position_differs = kruskal.test(nt_after_stall ~ g, data = df)$p.value,
         p_group_after_position = a$`Pr(>F)`[2])
}
confound <- map_dfr(levels(dd$condition), function(cn) {
  x <- dd %>% filter(condition == cn)
  bind_rows(
    confound_test(x %>% mutate(g2 = pool_small(family, protect = FAMILY_NA_LABEL)), "g2", "family", cn),
    confound_test(x %>% mutate(g2 = pool_small(genus_group, protect = GENUS_NA_LABEL)), "g2", "genus", cn),
    confound_test(x %>% mutate(g2 = pool_small(cm_class)), "g2", "CM class", cn),
    if (HAS_HOST) confound_test(x %>% filter(!multi_host, host_group != HOST_NA_LABEL) %>%
                                  mutate(g2 = pool_small(host_group)), "g2",
                                glue("host {HOST_LEVEL}, single-host sites"), cn) else NULL,
    if (HAS_HOST) confound_test(x %>% filter(family %in% SUBSET_FAMILIES, !multi_host) %>%
                                  mutate(g2 = pool_small(host_group, 2)), "g2",
                                glue("host, within {paste(SUBSET_FAMILIES, collapse='+')}"), cn) else NULL)
}) %>% mutate(across(starts_with("p_"), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write_csv(confound, file.path(OUTDIR, "confound_tests.csv")); knitr::kable(confound)
cat("p_position_differs not significant, or p_group_after_position significant, = the difference survives\n")

cat("\nSpearman correlation of stall fraction with nt of tile after the stall:\n")
print(dd %>% group_by(condition) %>%
        summarise(n = sum(!is.na(nt_after_stall)),
                  rho = round(cor(sf, nt_after_stall, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), 3),
                  median_nt_after_stall = median(nt_after_stall, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"))

fc <- dd %>% filter(!is.na(nt_after_stall)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(nt_after_stall, sf, colour = condition)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cond_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Stall fraction against position of the stall within its tile",
       subtitle = str_wrap(glue(
         "x = tile_end - stall_position, i.e. how much sequence follows the stall in the tile the site ",
         "was called in. treated_sf divides by that tile's reads, so a stall near the tile 3' end has a ",
         "smaller denominator. Diagnostic, not a result. {src_line(SF_COL, ' from ', SRC_SITES)}"), 115),
       x = "nt of tile after the stall", y = "stall fraction") + theme_fl
save_fig(fc, "sf_vs_position_in_tile", w = 9, h = 5); fc
```

## 6. Section 10 — Sensitivity: adjacent sites at merge distance 0

The tables were produced with `merge_distance 0`. The flaviLib log flags **66 site pairs within 1 nt at
10 mM and 41 at 1 mM** — about 9 % of sites — where a single stall whose 5' ends scatter by one base is
counted twice. The 20 nt tile step makes this likelier than in viromelib, where the same question is
decision 4. This is an open decision and has to be settled before the site count is quoted.

```{r sensitivity}
adj <- d %>% arrange(condition, plain_accession, stall_site_genomic_position) %>%
  group_by(condition, plain_accession) %>%
  mutate(gap_to_previous = stall_site_genomic_position - lag(stall_site_genomic_position)) %>%
  ungroup()
adj_tab <- map_dfr(c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10), function(nt)
  adj %>% group_by(condition) %>%
    summarise(merge_nt = nt, sites_at_0 = n(),
              pairs_within = sum(gap_to_previous <= nt, na.rm = TRUE),
              sites_after_merging = n() - sum(gap_to_previous <= nt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")) %>%
  arrange(condition, merge_nt)
write_csv(adj_tab, file.path(OUTDIR, "merge_distance_sensitivity.csv")); knitr::kable(adj_tab)
cat("\nAt merge distance", MERGE_NT, "nt the site count becomes:\n")
print(adj_tab %>% filter(merge_nt == MERGE_NT) %>% select(condition, sites_at_0, sites_after_merging))

write_csv(adj %>% filter(!is.na(gap_to_previous), gap_to_previous <= 1) %>%
            select(condition, site_id, plain_accession, organism, family, region,
                   stall_site_genomic_position, gap_to_previous, cm_class, sf, reps_passing),
          file.path(OUTDIR, "adjacent_sites_within_1nt.csv"))
cat("\nadjacent_sites_within_1nt.csv lists every member of a <=1 nt pair, for the merge-distance decision.\n")
```

## 7. Section 11 — Diagnostic: how much the reported stall fraction depends on tile choice

`apply_publication_cutoffs.py` picks a site's representative tile row (`is_site_representative`). This
re-takes the stall fraction from the tile with the **most** sequence after the stall — the opposite end of
the confound in section 9 — to show how much the reported value depends on that choice. Not a figure.

```{r interior}
tile_files <- map_chr(CONDITIONS, tiles_path)
if (all(file.exists(tile_files))) {
  tr <- map2_dfr(CONDITIONS, tile_files, function(cond, p) {
    x <- suppressWarnings(read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal"))
    x <- x[, !duplicated(names(x))]
    TR_SF <- c(SF_COL, "median_treated_sf")[c(SF_COL, "median_treated_sf") %in% names(x)][1]
    x %>% transmute(site_id, condition = unname(COND_LABELS[cond]),
                    sf_tile = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[TR_SF]])),
                    nt_after_tile = tile_end - stall_position,
                    is_rep = str_to_lower(as.character(is_site_representative)) %in% c("true", "1"))
  })
  int <- tr %>% group_by(condition, site_id) %>%
    summarise(n_tiles = n(),
              sf_interior = sf_tile[which.max(nt_after_tile)],
              sf_representative = if (any(is_rep)) sf_tile[which(is_rep)[1]] else NA_real_,
              .groups = "drop")
  cmp <- dd %>% left_join(int, by = c("site_id", "condition")) %>%
    mutate(n_tiles = coalesce(n_tiles, 1L), sf_interior = coalesce(sf_interior, sf))
  # the representative row in the tile table should be the row the sites table reports
  mism <- cmp %>% filter(!is.na(sf_representative), abs(sf - sf_representative) > 1e-9)
  cat(nrow(mism), "sites where the sites table's stall fraction differs from the tile row flagged",
      "is_site_representative (expected 0)\n")
  multi <- cmp %>% filter(n_tiles >= 2)
  print(multi %>% group_by(condition) %>%
          summarise(sites_2plus_tiles = n(),
                    differs_from_most_interior_tile = sum(abs(sf - sf_interior) > 1e-9),
                    median_sf_reported = round(median(sf), 3),
                    median_sf_most_interior = round(median(sf_interior), 3), .groups = "drop"))
  write_csv(cmp %>% select(condition, site_id, family, genus_group, sf, sf_interior,
                           sf_representative, n_tiles),
            file.path(OUTDIR, "diagnostic_sf_reported_vs_interior.csv"))
} else {
  cat("NOT FOUND:", paste(basename(tile_files[!file.exists(tile_files)]), collapse = ", "),
      "\n  Section 11 skipped.\n")
}
```

## 8. Supporting tables and manifest

```{r tables}
# Not a figure. A .cm_hit is recorded only where the model matches AT the stall, so "CM hits are near the
# stop codon" is true by construction. The non-circular question is how many stalls with NO known model
# fall where the known ones do. Needs distance_from_stop.
if (HAS_STOP_DATA) {
  ds2 <- d %>% filter(!is.na(distance_from_stop)) %>%
    mutate(cm_hit = if_else(cm_class == "No hit", "No CM hit", "CM hit"))
  known_win <- ds2 %>% filter(cm_hit == "CM hit") %>% group_by(condition, region) %>%
    summarise(lo = quantile(distance_from_stop, .25), hi = quantile(distance_from_stop, .75),
              n_known = n(), .groups = "drop")
  nohit <- ds2 %>% filter(cm_hit == "No CM hit") %>% left_join(known_win, by = c("condition", "region")) %>%
    mutate(in_window = !is.na(lo) & distance_from_stop >= lo & distance_from_stop <= hi)
  win_tab <- nohit %>% group_by(condition, region) %>%
    summarise(n_nohit = n(), n_known = first(n_known),
              known_IQR = glue("{round(first(lo))} to {round(first(hi))}"),
              n_in_window = sum(in_window), pct_in_window = round(100 * mean(in_window), 1),
              .groups = "drop")
  write_csv(win_tab, file.path(OUTDIR, "nohit_in_known_window.csv")); knitr::kable(win_tab)
  write_csv(nohit %>% filter(in_window) %>%
              select(condition, site_id, organism, family, genus_group, region,
                     distance_from_stop, sf),
            file.path(OUTDIR, "nohit_inside_known_window.csv"))
}

# Which organisms carry sites in the subset family, and in which conditions
write_csv(d %>% filter(family %in% SUBSET_FAMILIES) %>%
            group_by(plain_accession, organism, genus_group) %>%
            summarise(n_sites = n(), conditions = paste(sort(unique(as.character(condition))),
                                                        collapse = " + "), .groups = "drop") %>%
            arrange(genus_group, organism),
          file.path(OUTDIR, "subset_accessions.csv"))
```
